docs.title: Ligase
docs.text: Type-safe, reproducible computational biology pipelines. A Rust core with a Python surface.

docs.title: The idea
docs.text:
Biological data types carry dimensions — organism, reference build, coordinate system, sample set — and the engine refuses to connect steps whose dimensions do not match, the way a physics engine refuses to add metres to seconds.

The worst comp bio bugs are silent. hg19 against hg38. 0-based against 1-based. chr1 against 1. Sample IDs that shifted by one somewhere in a join. None of these crash; they produce plausible numbers that are wrong. Workflow managers like Snakemake and Nextflow move files between steps very well, but they do not understand what is in them. Ligase does, and it checks before it computes.

pipe.check()      # type-checks dimensions; no compute
pipe.run()        # parallel, cached, per-sample fan-out
pipe.methods()    # generated methods paragraph + reproducibility bundle

When a pipeline is wrong, you should find out in milliseconds rather than after an overnight run:

DimensionError in step `call`:
  aln.reference = HXB2 (from BAM @SQ header)
  ref.reference = hg38
  These must match. Did you pass the wrong reference?

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Pre-alpha, at v0.1's last milestone. M0 (scaffold), M1 (types and dimensions), M2 (the graph), M3 (execution and cache), M4 (semantic hashing and early cutoff), M5 (provenance) and M6 (validation) are complete.

The reference pipeline now interprets as well as computes: its resistance calls reproduce published Stanford HIVdb results exactly at the 15% and 5% thresholds, with every remaining discrepancy explained. Three remain at the 2% threshold, where there were nine: six were codons read from a VCF, which carries no phasing, and went when codons started being read from the haplotypes the reads carry.

You can write a pipeline of annotated steps, have the whole graph type-checked without running any of it, be told every mistake at once, and then run it — in parallel, cached, one branch per sample:

import ligase as lg
from ligase.types import Alignment, Reads, Reference, Variants


@lg.step(tool="minimap2")
def align(reads: Reads, ref: Reference) -> Alignment:
    return lg.sh("minimap2 -ax sr {ref} {reads.r1} {reads.r2} | samtools sort -o {out}")


@lg.step(tool="bcftools")
def call(aln: Alignment, ref: Reference, min_freq: float = 0.01) -> Variants:
    return lg.sh("bcftools mpileup -f {ref} {aln} | bcftools call -mv -Oz -o {out}")


hxb2 = lg.reference("data/refs/HXB2.fasta", organism="HIV-1", build="HXB2")
samples = lg.samples("data/runs/*.fastq.gz", paired=True)

pipe = lg.Pipeline(samples.map(lambda s: call(align(s, hxb2), hxb2)))
pipe.check()        # type-checks every step. Nothing runs.

$ ligase check
checked 8 steps in pipeline.py

DimensionError in step `call` (sample SRR32217714):
  aln.reference = HXB2 (from step `align`)
  ref.reference = hg38 (from FASTA contigs: data/refs/hg38.fasta)
  Contig `K03455.1` is not in hg38.
  These must match. Did you pass the wrong reference?
  The same problem affects 3 other samples: SRR32217715, SRR32217716, SRR32217726.

4 errors in 4 steps.

The step bodies never ran, aln.reference came out of a step that does not exist yet, and a problem that hit the whole cohort is stated once with every affected sample named.

Point it at the right reference and it runs:

$ ligase run
running 12 steps in pipeline.py

ran       `align` (sample SRR8525904)        4.5s
ran       `call` (sample SRR8525904)         513ms
ran       `resistance` (sample SRR8525904)   3ms
...

12 steps: 12 ran.

Run it again and nothing is recomputed, because a step's key is built from its code, its parameters, its inputs' contents and its tools' versions — and none of those moved:

$ ligase run
cached    `align` for SRR8525904, SRR8525908, SRR8525920, SRR8525942
cached    `call` for SRR8525904, SRR8525908, SRR8525920, SRR8525942
cached    `resistance` for SRR8525904, SRR8525908, SRR8525920, SRR8525942

12 steps: 12 from cache.

Change min_freq and only call and resistance come back. Add a sample and only that sample is processed.

Run the aligner again on eight cores instead of one and it reruns — a thread count is a parameter, and nothing can know in advance that it will not change an answer — but the alignments come out the same, so nothing below it is recomputed:

$ ligase run
ran       `align` (sample SRR8525904)   3.3s
ran       `align` (sample SRR8525908)   6.9s
ran       `align` (sample SRR8525920)   3.7s
ran       `align` (sample SRR8525942)   6.0s
skipped   `call` for SRR8525904, SRR8525908, SRR8525920, SRR8525942
skipped   `resistance` for SRR8525904, SRR8525908, SRR8525920, SRR8525942

12 steps: 4 ran, 8 skipped.

"The same" is not byte equality — minimap2 writes -t 8 and the output path into the BAM's @PG line — but what the file means: its records sorted and the fields recording when and how it was made dropped. And when you want the opposite question answered, ligase audit <step> runs a step twice and says whether it repeats.

And when you need to say how the results were produced, ligase methods does — naming the version every tool actually ran at, every parameter as it was hashed, the reference by accession and checksum, and the papers to cite:

$ ligase methods
`align` ran on 4 samples (SRR8525904, SRR8525908, SRR8525920, SRR8525942)
with minimap2 2.31-r1302 and samtools 1.24, as `minimap2 -t {threads} -ax sr
{ref} {reads.r1} {reads.r2} | samtools sort -@ {threads} -o {out}`, with
threads = 4, against the HXB2 reference (K03455.1, 9719 bp, MD5
c66838498aab02f786a6ec2f2d62cdc1).

It can say that about a run where nothing was recomputed, which is the point: the command is recorded when a step runs, because since M4 it is not in the output's hash and a cache hit can no longer prove it. --bundle packages all of it so someone else can check the results, and --verify is that check.

M6 (validation) is done: the resistance calls agree with the published ones, and what does not agree says why. See milestones for the order and the acceptance test for each step.

Load a reference FASTA, inferring its contigs.

Each contig's MD5 is computed here, over the uppercased sequence, as the SAM specification defines @SQ M5. Computing it ourselves is what lets us check an aligner's claim about which reference it used.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The FASTA, optionally gzipped.

required organism str | None

The organism, e.g. HIV-1. A FASTA cannot record this.

None build str | None

A human label such as HXB2 or hg38. Display only -- reference identity never rests on a label, so two files both labelled hg38 still fail to match if their contigs disagree.

None

The loaded reference.

Raises:

Type Description LoadError

def reference(
    path: str,
    *,
    organism: str | None = None,
    build: str | None = None,
) -> Reference:
    """Load a reference FASTA, inferring its contigs.

    Each contig's MD5 is computed here, over the uppercased sequence, as the
    SAM specification defines `@SQ M5`. Computing it ourselves is what lets
    us check an aligner's claim about which reference it used.

    Args:
        path: The FASTA, optionally gzipped.
        organism: The organism, e.g. `HIV-1`. A FASTA cannot record this.
        build: A human label such as `HXB2` or `hg38`. Display only --
            reference identity never rests on a label, so two files both
            labelled `hg38` still fail to match if their contigs disagree.

    Returns:
        The loaded reference.

    Raises:
        LoadError: If the file cannot be read or is not a FASTA.
    """
    return Reference(_core.load_reference(path, organism, build))

Load sequencing reads, inferring what a FASTQ can tell us.

def reads(
    r1: str,
    r2: str | None = None,
    *,
    organism: str | None = None,
    sample: str | None = None,
) -> Reads:
    """Load sequencing reads, inferring what a FASTQ can tell us.

    The quality encoding comes from the observed score range, and comes back
    unknown rather than guessed when the scores fall in the range Phred+33
    and Phred+64 share. Guessing would shift every quality value by 31,
    which no downstream tool would notice.

    Args:
        r1: The reads, or the first mate of a pair. Optionally gzipped.
        r2: The second mate, if the reads are paired.
        organism: The organism. A FASTQ does not record it.
        sample: The sample identifier, overriding the one taken from the
            filename.

    Returns:
        The loaded reads.

    Raises:
        LoadError: If a file cannot be read or is not a FASTQ.
    """
    samples = None if sample is None else [sample]
    return Reads(_core.load_reads(r1, r2, organism, samples))

def alignment(
    path: str,
    *,
    organism: str | None = None,
    build: str | None = None,
    samples: list[str] | None = None,
) -> Alignment:
    """Load a SAM or BAM, inferring dimensions from its header.

    Both containers yield identical dimensions: a lossless
    ``samtools view -b`` changes nothing biological.

    Args:
        path: The alignment file.
        organism: The organism. SAM and BAM headers do not record it.
        build: A human label for the reference build. Display only.
        samples: The sample identifiers, overriding the `@RG SM` tags.

    Returns:

    """

intervals(
    path: str,
    *,
    format: str | None = None,
    organism: str | None = None,
    build: str | None = None,
) -> Intervals

Load genomic intervals from a BED or GFF, inferring what they say.

The coordinate convention comes from the format — BED is 0-based half-open, GFF and GTF are 1-based closed — and that is the point: a tool handed the wrong one produces results that are off by one base and look fine.

Contigs come from the records, so they carry no length and no checksum. They are still compared against a reference by name, because comparing what is present is what makes these files checkable at all.

Parameters:

The BED, GFF3 or GTF, optionally gzipped.

required format str | None

None organism str | None

The organism. An interval file does not record it.

None build str | None

A human label for the reference build. Display only.

None

def intervals(
    path: str,
    *,
    format: str | None = None,  # noqa: A002 - the file's format, not a builtin
    organism: str | None = None,
    build: str | None = None,
) -> Intervals:
    """Load genomic intervals from a BED or GFF, inferring what they say.

    The coordinate convention comes from the format — BED is 0-based
    half-open, GFF and GTF are 1-based closed — and that is the point: a
    tool handed the wrong one produces results that are off by one base and
    look fine.

    Contigs come from the records, so they carry no length and no checksum.
    They are still compared against a reference by name, because comparing
    what is present is what makes these files checkable at all.

    Args:
        path: The BED, GFF3 or GTF, optionally gzipped.
        format: `bed`, `gff`, `gff3` or `gtf`, when the filename does not
            say. A format is never guessed: guessing it wrong shifts every
            interval by a base.
        organism: The organism. An interval file does not record it.
        build: A human label for the reference build. Display only.

    Returns:
        The loaded intervals.

    Raises:
        LoadError: If the file cannot be read, is not in the format given,
            or its format cannot be told from its name.
    """
    return Intervals(_core.load_intervals(path, format, organism, build))

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
A graph of steps, built from its outputs and checked before it runs.

Construction walks back from the outputs through the handles each step was given, so a file passed to two steps becomes one node rather than two. Nothing is executed and nothing is read: the graph is built from signatures and from the dimensions the inputs were loaded with.

Source code in python/ligase/graph.py 
class Pipeline:
    """A graph of steps, built from its outputs and checked before it runs.

    Construction walks back from the outputs through the handles each step
    was given, so a file passed to two steps becomes one node rather than
    two. Nothing is executed and nothing is read: the graph is built from
    signatures and from the dimensions the inputs were loaded with.
    """

    __slots__ = ("_graph", "_handles", "_outputs", "_roots")

    def __init__(self, outputs: Dataset | Iterable[Dataset]) -> None:
        """Build the graph that produces these outputs.

        Args:
            outputs: One handle, or an iterable of them — what
                `samples.map(...)` returns. A type checker sees handles as
                the data types their steps return, which is how a mis-wired
                pipeline is caught before `check()` ever runs.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If no outputs were given.
            TypeError: If a step was passed something that is neither
                loaded data nor another step's output.
        """
        self._graph = _core.Graph()
        self._handles: dict[int, StepOutput] = {}
        self._outputs: list[object] = list(_as_outputs(outputs))
        if not self._outputs:
            raise ValueError(
                "a Pipeline needs at least one output; pass the handle a step "
                "returned, or the list `samples.map(...)` gives you"
            )
        # Keyed by identity: two datasets loaded from the same file are two
        # nodes, because the user wrote them as two.
        placed: dict[int, int] = {}
        pinned: list[object] = []
        self._roots = [self._place(out, placed, pinned) for out in self._outputs]

    def _place(
        self, value: object, placed: dict[int, int], pinned: list[object]
    ) -> int:
        existing = placed.get(id(value))
        if existing is not None:
            return existing

        if isinstance(value, StepOutput):
            arguments = [
                (parameter.name, parameter.kind, self._place(given, placed, pinned))
                for parameter, given in _checked_inputs(value)
            ]
            node = self._graph.add_step(
                value.step.name,
                value.step.output,
                arguments,
                value.step.coordinates,
            )
            value._attach(self._graph, node)
            # A run asks each handle how its output is produced, so the
            # graph's nodes have to lead back to the handles that made them.
            self._handles[node] = value
        elif isinstance(value, Dataset):
            node = self._graph.add_input(value.kind.lower(), value._core)
        else:
            raise TypeError(
                f"a step was given {value!r}, which is neither loaded data nor "
                "another step's output"
            )

        placed[id(value)] = node
        # `id` is only unique while the object lives, so keep them all alive.
        pinned.append(value)
        return node

    @property
    def steps(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """The steps this pipeline runs, in dependency order."""
        return tuple(self._graph.step_names(self._roots))

    def report(self) -> Report:
        """Check every step and return everything found, without raising."""
        raw, summary, text = self._graph.check(self._roots)
        return Report(build(raw), summary, text)

    def errors(self) -> list[CheckError]:
        """Return every problem in this pipeline, without raising.

        Returns:
            One error per problem, in the order the steps run. Empty when
            the pipeline is consistent. Nothing is computed.
        """
        return self.report().errors

    def check(self) -> None:
        """Type-check the whole pipeline. Nothing is computed.

        Every problem is found before anything is raised, so the raised
        error's `errors` attribute holds all of them.

        Raises:
            CheckError: If anything is wrong. The subclass says what:
                `DimensionError` and its own subclasses for data that
                disagrees, `StepTypeError` for a step wired to the wrong
                kind of data.
        """
        errors = self.errors()
        if errors:
            raise errors[0]

    def run(
        self,
        *,
        jobs: int | None = None,
        force: bool = False,
        cache: str | Path | None = None,
    ) -> RunReport:
        """Check the pipeline, then compute whatever is not already known.

        The pipeline is checked first, every time: running an unchecked
        pipeline is how an overnight run ends in a dimension error.

        A step runs when something that could change its result has changed
        — its code, a parameter, an input's contents, or the version of a
        tool it calls — and not otherwise. Independent steps run at once,
        and a step whose rerun produced the same output as before leaves
        everything below it alone.

        Args:
            jobs: How many steps may run at once. Defaults to the number of
                cores.
            force: Run every step, cache or no cache. For the one case the
                cache cannot see: a file rewritten in place, keeping its
                length and its timestamp.
            cache: Where to keep the cache. Defaults to `.ligase` under the
                working directory.

        Returns:
            What every step did, and where its output is.

        Raises:
            CheckError: If the pipeline does not type-check. Nothing runs.
            RunError: If any step failed. Everything that did succeed is on
                the error's `report`, which for a cohort is usually most of
                it.
        """
        self.check()
        tasks, callbacks = self._plan()
        directory = Path(cache) if cache is not None else Path.cwd() / CACHE_DIR

        finished, failed, summary, text, counted = self._graph.run(
            self._roots,
            tasks,
            str(directory),
            callbacks,
            jobs,
            force,
        )

        steps = []
        for (
            node,
            name,
            outcome,
            key,
            digest,
            canonical,
            output,
            duration,
            notes,
        ) in finished:
            # Tell the handle where its output landed, so a later
            # `lg.handle(x).path` and the next run's bodies can read it.
            produced = self._handles.get(node)
            if produced is not None:
                produced._produced = output
            steps.append(
                StepRun(
                    step=name,
                    sample=self._sample(node),
                    outcome=outcome,
                    output=output,
                    key=key,
                    hash=digest,
                    canonical=canonical,
                    duration_ms=duration,
                    node=node,
                    notes=tuple(notes),
                )
            )

        hashed, prefiltered, canonicalised = counted
        report = RunReport(
            steps=steps,
            failures=[
                StepFailure(
                    step=name,
                    sample=self._sample(node),
                    message=message,
                    node=node,
                )
                for node, name, message in failed
            ],
            summary=summary,
            text=text,
            hashed=hashed,
            prefiltered=prefiltered,
            canonicalised=canonicalised,
        )
        if report.failures:
            raise RunError(report)
        return report

    def audit(
        self,
        step: str,
        *,
        sample: str | None = None,
        jobs: int | None = None,
        cache: str | Path | None = None,
    ) -> AuditReport:
        """Run one step twice and report whether it is reproducible.

        The pipeline is run first, normally and through the cache, so that
        the step being audited has its inputs. Then each node of that step
        is run twice more, into scratch files that are thrown away, and the
        two outputs are compared both as bytes and as meaning.

        Three verdicts, because two would not do. A step whose bytes move
        while its result does not — which is every tool that records its own
        command line — is `reproducible`, not a failure. Only a step whose
        *result* moves is `not reproducible`.

        Args:
            step: The step's name, as written. Under per-sample fan-out
                there is one node of it per sample, and all of them are
                audited.
            sample: Audit only the node for this sample.
            jobs: How many steps may run at once in the preliminary run.
                The audited steps are taken in turn whatever this says, so
                that the durations reported mean something.
            cache: Where to keep the cache. Defaults to `.ligase` under the
                working directory.

        Returns:
            What two runs of each node showed.

        Raises:
            CheckError: If the pipeline does not type-check. Nothing runs.
            ValueError: If no step of that name is in the pipeline, or no
                node of it is for that sample.
        """
        self.check()
        tasks, callbacks = self._plan()
        directory = Path(cache) if cache is not None else Path.cwd() / CACHE_DIR

        audited, failed, verdict, summary, text = self._graph.audit(
            self._roots,
            tasks,
            str(directory),
            callbacks,
            (step, sample),
            jobs,
        )

        return AuditReport(
            steps=[
                StepAudit(
                    step=name,
                    sample=self._sample(node),
                    scope=scope,
                    verdict=step_verdict,
                    first=first,
                    second=second,
                    first_canonical=first_canonical,
                    second_canonical=second_canonical,
                    first_duration_ms=first_ms,
                    second_duration_ms=second_ms,
                    node=node,
                )
                for (
                    node,
                    name,
                    scope,
                    step_verdict,
                    first,
                    second,
                    first_canonical,
                    second_canonical,
                    first_ms,
                    second_ms,
                ) in audited
            ],
            failures=[
                StepFailure(
                    step=name,
                    sample=self._sample(node),
                    message=message,
                    node=node,
                )
                for node, name, message in failed
            ],
            verdict=verdict,
            summary=summary,
            text=text,
        )

    def methods(
        self,
        *,
        bundle: str | Path | None = None,
        verify: str | Path | None = None,
        include: Sequence[str | Path] = (),
        jobs: int | None = None,
        cache: str | Path | None = None,
    ) -> Methods:
        """Say how this pipeline's results were produced.

        The pipeline is run first, normally and through the cache, because a
        provenance record is filed under a step's key and computing keys is
        what a run does. A pipeline already computed costs a cache lookup
        per step, not a recomputation.

        What comes back names, for every step: the tools and the versions
        they ran at, the parameters as they were hashed, the command as
        written, and every reference by accession and checksum. A step whose
        output predates provenance is reported as a gap rather than left
        out, because nothing can reconstruct how it was produced — the
        command that would have said so is deliberately not in the hash.

        Args:
            bundle: Write a reproducibility bundle into this directory.
            verify: Check the bundle in this directory against what this
                machine just produced, and report where they differ.
            include: Files to copy into the bundle as they are, such as the
                pipeline itself.
            jobs: How many steps may run at once in the run beforehand.
            cache: Where to keep the cache. Defaults to `.ligase` under the
                working directory.

        Returns:
            How every step was produced, with the bundle written and the
            verification done, where either was asked for.

        Raises:
            CheckError: If the pipeline does not type-check. Nothing runs.
            RuntimeError: If a step failed, since a pipeline that did not
                finish has no methods section to write; or if a bundle
                cannot be written.
            ValueError: If the directory to verify against is not a bundle.
        """
        self.check()
        tasks, callbacks = self._plan()
        directory = Path(cache) if cache is not None else Path.cwd() / CACHE_DIR

        described, written, checked = self._graph.methods(
            self._roots,
            tasks,
            str(directory),
            callbacks,
            (
                None if bundle is None else str(bundle),
                None if verify is None else str(verify),
                [str(path) for path in include],
            ),
            jobs,
        )

        (
            groups,
            gaps,
            references,
            citations,
            uncited,
            engine,
            platform,
            summary,
            text,
        ) = described

        return Methods(
            steps=[
                StepMethods(
                    step=step,
                    nodes=nodes,
                    scopes=list(scopes),
                    scope_kind=scope_kind,
                    tools=list(tools),
                    parameters=list(parameters),
                    command=command,
                )
                for (
                    step,
                    nodes,
                    scopes,
                    scope_kind,
                    tools,
                    parameters,
                    command,
                ) in groups
            ],
            gaps=[
                MethodsGap(step=step, scopes=list(scopes), nodes=nodes)
                for step, scopes, nodes in gaps
            ],
            references=[
                PinnedReference(
                    param=param,
                    path=path,
                    build=build,
                    accession=accession,
                    contigs=contigs,
                    length=length,
                    checksum=checksum,
                    fingerprint=fingerprint,
                )
                for (
                    param,
                    path,
                    build,
                    accession,
                    contigs,
                    length,
                    checksum,
                    fingerprint,
                ) in references
            ],
            citations=list(citations),
            uncited=list(uncited),
            engine=engine,
            platform=platform,
            summary=summary,
            text=text,
            bundle=_bundle(written),
            verification=_verification(checked),
        )

    def _plan(self) -> tuple[list[_Task], list[_Callback]]:
        """Ask every step how its output is produced, before anything runs.

        This is the one moment a step body is called, and it is called for
        its *answer* rather than for its effect: a command to render, or a
        function to call later. Nothing has been computed, so a body that
        reaches for an input's contents here is a body that cannot work.
        """
        tasks: list[_Task] = []
        callbacks: list[_Callback] = []

        for node, produced in sorted(self._handles.items()):
            recipe = _recipe(produced)
            callback: int | None = None
            command: str | None = None
            if isinstance(recipe, Shell):
                command = recipe.command
            else:
                callback = len(callbacks)
                callbacks.append(_bind(recipe, produced))

            step = produced.step
            tasks.append(
                (
                    node,
                    _source(step.function),
                    command,
                    callback,
                    list(step.tools),
                    [
                        (parameter.name, repr(produced.arguments[parameter.name]))
                        for parameter in step.plain_parameters
                    ],
                    list(step.citations),
                )
            )

        return tasks, callbacks

    def _sample(self, node: int) -> str | None:
        """The one sample a node stands for, if it stands for exactly one."""
        found = self._graph.dataset(node)
        if found is None:
            return None
        samples = found.samples()
        if samples is None or len(samples) != 1:
            return None
        return samples[0]

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        """How many nodes the graph holds, inputs included."""
        return len(self._graph)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Identify the pipeline by its size."""
        return f"<Pipeline {len(self.steps)} steps, {len(self)} nodes>"

def __init__(self, outputs: Dataset | Iterable[Dataset]) -> None:
    """Build the graph that produces these outputs.

    Args:
        outputs: One handle, or an iterable of them — what
            `samples.map(...)` returns. A type checker sees handles as
            the data types their steps return, which is how a mis-wired
            pipeline is caught before `check()` ever runs.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If no outputs were given.
        TypeError: If a step was passed something that is neither
            loaded data nor another step's output.
    """
    self._graph = _core.Graph()
    self._handles: dict[int, StepOutput] = {}
    self._outputs: list[object] = list(_as_outputs(outputs))
    if not self._outputs:
        raise ValueError(
            "a Pipeline needs at least one output; pass the handle a step "
            "returned, or the list `samples.map(...)` gives you"
        )
    # Keyed by identity: two datasets loaded from the same file are two
    # nodes, because the user wrote them as two.
    placed: dict[int, int] = {}
    pinned: list[object] = []
    self._roots = [self._place(out, placed, pinned) for out in self._outputs]

def check(self) -> None:
    """Type-check the whole pipeline. Nothing is computed.

    Every problem is found before anything is raised, so the raised
    error's `errors` attribute holds all of them.

    Raises:
        CheckError: If anything is wrong. The subclass says what:
            `DimensionError` and its own subclasses for data that
            disagrees, `StepTypeError` for a step wired to the wrong
            kind of data.
    """
    errors = self.errors()
    if errors:
        raise errors[0]

def run(
    self,
    *,
    jobs: int | None = None,
    force: bool = False,
    cache: str | Path | None = None,
) -> RunReport:
    """Check the pipeline, then compute whatever is not already known.

    The pipeline is checked first, every time: running an unchecked
    pipeline is how an overnight run ends in a dimension error.

    A step runs when something that could change its result has changed
    — its code, a parameter, an input's contents, or the version of a
    tool it calls — and not otherwise. Independent steps run at once,
    and a step whose rerun produced the same output as before leaves
    everything below it alone.

    Args:
        jobs: How many steps may run at once. Defaults to the number of
            cores.
        force: Run every step, cache or no cache. For the one case the
            cache cannot see: a file rewritten in place, keeping its
            length and its timestamp.
        cache: Where to keep the cache. Defaults to `.ligase` under the
            working directory.

    Returns:
        What every step did, and where its output is.

    Raises:
        CheckError: If the pipeline does not type-check. Nothing runs.
        RunError: If any step failed. Everything that did succeed is on
            the error's `report`, which for a cohort is usually most of
            it.
    """
    self.check()
    tasks, callbacks = self._plan()
    directory = Path(cache) if cache is not None else Path.cwd() / CACHE_DIR

    finished, failed, summary, text, counted = self._graph.run(
        self._roots,
        tasks,
        str(directory),
        callbacks,
        jobs,
        force,
    )

    steps = []
    for (
        node,
        name,
        outcome,
        key,
        digest,
        canonical,
        output,
        duration,
        notes,
    ) in finished:
        # Tell the handle where its output landed, so a later
        # `lg.handle(x).path` and the next run's bodies can read it.
        produced = self._handles.get(node)
        if produced is not None:
            produced._produced = output
        steps.append(
            StepRun(
                step=name,
                sample=self._sample(node),
                outcome=outcome,
                output=output,
                key=key,
                hash=digest,
                canonical=canonical,
                duration_ms=duration,
                node=node,
                notes=tuple(notes),
            )
        )

    hashed, prefiltered, canonicalised = counted
    report = RunReport(
        steps=steps,
        failures=[
            StepFailure(
                step=name,
                sample=self._sample(node),
                message=message,
                node=node,
            )
            for node, name, message in failed
        ],
        summary=summary,
        text=text,
        hashed=hashed,
        prefiltered=prefiltered,
        canonicalised=canonicalised,
    )
    if report.failures:
        raise RunError(report)
    return report

class Step(Generic[P, R]):
    """A function that records a call instead of running.

    Attributes:
        function: The undecorated callable. A run calls it once, before
            anything executes, to ask how the output is produced.
        tool: The external tools the step shells out to, as they were given.
        tools: Those tools as a tuple, whose versions join the cache key.
        coordinates: The coordinate convention the step writes, for the one
            output kind that does not imply one.
        citations: References the step asks to be cited by.
    """

    __slots__ = (
        "_signature",
        "citations",
        "coordinates",
        "function",
        "output",
        "parameters",
        "tool",
        "tools",
    )

    def __init__(
        self,
        function: Callable[P, R],
        *,
        tool: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
        coordinates: str | None = None,
        cite: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Read a function's signature, refusing one a graph cannot use."""
        self.function = function
        self.tool = tool
        self.tools = _tools(tool)
        self.coordinates = coordinates
        self.citations = _citations(cite)
        self._signature = inspect.signature(function)
        self.output = _output_kind(function)
        self.parameters = _parameters(function, self._signature)

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """The step's name, as it appears in messages."""
        return self.function.__name__

    @property
    def dataset_parameters(self) -> tuple[Parameter, ...]:
        """The parameters that take data, in declaration order.

        Order matters: a dimension is inherited from the first argument that
        states it.
        """
        return tuple(p for p in self.parameters if p.kind is not None)

    @property
    def plain_parameters(self) -> tuple[Parameter, ...]:
        """The parameters that take plain values, in declaration order."""
        return tuple(p for p in self.parameters if p.kind is None)

    def __call__(self, *args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> R:
        """Record a call and return a handle on what it would produce.

        The body is not run. Missing or surplus arguments still fail here,
        exactly as they would for the undecorated function.
        """
        bound = self._signature.bind(*args, **kwargs)
        bound.apply_defaults()
        # The handle is not really an `R`. It stands in for one, which is
        # what lets a type checker follow a pipeline it will never run.
        return cast("R", StepOutput(self, dict(bound.arguments)))

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Identify the step by name and what it produces."""
        return f"<Step {self.name} -> {self.output}>"

def step(
    function: Callable[P, R] | None = None,
    /,
    *,
    tool: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    coordinates: str | None = None,
    cite: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
) -> Step[P, R] | Callable[[Callable[P, R]], Step[P, R]]:
    """Make a function a pipeline step, without ever running it.

    The signature is read once, here. Each parameter annotated with a Ligase
    data type becomes an edge in the graph; the rest are plain values. The
    return annotation is what says the step produces an `Alignment`, since
    nothing will ask the body.

    Args:
        function: The function to decorate, when used bare as `@lg.step`.
        tool: The external tool the step shells out to, e.g. `minimap2`,
            or several of them: `tool=("minimap2", "samtools")` for a body
            that pipes one into the other. Each one's `--version` joins the
            cache key, so an upgrade that changes a result reruns the steps
            it could have changed.
        coordinates: The coordinate convention the step writes, one of
            `"0-based half-open"` or `"1-based closed"`. Only meaningful for
            a step that produces `Intervals`: alignments and variant calls
            are 1-based closed by specification, while a tool that writes
            BED from a VCF changes the convention and must say so.
        cite: How the step asks to be cited, as one reference or several.
            `ligase methods` knows the reference pipeline's own tools; a
            step using anything else names its reference here, or the
            methods section reports that tool as uncited. A citation never
            joins the cache key — it cannot change a result, so adding one
            must not rerun anything.

    Returns:
        A `Step`, which a type checker sees as the function it decorated.

    Raises:
        StepDefinitionError: If the signature is one a graph cannot use —
            an unannotated parameter, a missing or non-Ligase return
            annotation, or `*args`/`**kwargs`.
        ValueError: If `coordinates` is not one of the two conventions, or
            a tool was named as an empty string.
    """
    if coordinates is not None and coordinates not in COORDINATES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"`{coordinates}` is not a coordinate system; expected "
            + " or ".join(COORDINATES)
        )

    def decorate(inner: Callable[P, R]) -> Step[P, R]:
        return Step(inner, tool=tool, coordinates=coordinates, cite=cite)

    if function is None:
        return decorate
    return decorate(function)

def sh(command: str) -> R:  # type: ignore[type-var]
    """Produce the output by running a shell command.

    The command is not run here and the string is not formatted here: the
    engine fills it in once it knows where the inputs are, and runs it at
    whatever width the machine allows.

    Placeholders name the step's own parameters:

    - `{ref}` — the file bound to the parameter `ref`.
    - `{reads.r1}`, `{reads.r2}` — the mates of a paired input.
    - `{min_freq}` — a plain parameter's value.
    - `{out}` — the file the step must write. A step that writes anywhere
      else produces nothing, as far as the engine is concerned.

    Every value is substituted as exactly one shell word, so a path with a
    space in it stays one path. For a literal brace — an `awk '{{print $1}}'`
    — double it.

    Args:
        command: The command, with placeholders.

    Returns:
        A recipe, typed as the data the step declares, so a body reads as
        `return lg.sh(...)` under a `-> Alignment` annotation.
    """
    # Typed as the step's own return so that user pipelines type-check as
    # written; at runtime it is a `Shell`, which is what the engine wants.
    return Shell(command)  # type: ignore[return-value]

Produce the output in Python, by writing the file yourself.

function is called with the path to write to. It is the one thing in a run that takes the GIL, so steps written this way do not run in parallel with each other — which is the right trade for an interpretation step and the wrong one for anything that does real work. Prefer lg.sh.

A body may also return what it noticed about its own work, as Noticed pairs of a note's code and what it is about. That is the only way such a thing can be said: an assumption the work rested on need leave no trace in the file it wrote — a resistance reading made without coverage writes the same report a fully covered one does — so the body says it and the engine carries it into the run report, provenance, a bundle and the methods section. def handle(output: object) -> StepOutput:
    """The handle behind what a step returned.

    A type checker sees `align(reads, ref)` as returning an `Alignment`,
    which is what lets it follow a pipeline and catch a mis-wired one while
    you are still editing. At runtime the value is a `StepOutput` — data that
    does not exist yet — and this is how to reach it without writing a cast
    at every call site.

    Args:
        output: What a step returned.

    Returns:
        The handle, with its step, its arguments and (once a `Pipeline` has
        been built) the dimensions the output will carry.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If this is not a step's output — loaded data, say, which
            is already the thing itself.
    """
    if not isinstance(output, StepOutput):
        raise TypeError(
            f"{output!r} is not a step's output; only a value a step returned "
            "has a handle behind it"
        )
    return output

Ligase: type-safe, reproducible computational biology pipelines.

Biological data types carry dimensions (organism, reference build, coordinate system, sample set), and the engine refuses to connect steps whose dimensions do not match -- like units in physics.

>>> import ligase as lg
>>> from ligase.types import Alignment, Reads, Reference
>>> hxb2 = lg.reference("refs/HXB2.fasta", organism="HIV-1", build="HXB2")
>>> samples = lg.samples("data/*.fastq.gz", paired=True)
>>> @lg.step(tool="minimap2")
... def align(reads: Reads, ref: Reference) -> Alignment: ...
>>> pipe = lg.Pipeline(samples.map(lambda s: align(s, hxb2)))
>>> pipe.check()   # type-checks every step; nothing runs
>>> pipe.run()     # parallel, cached, per-sample fan-out

def check_step(step: str, bindings: Mapping[str, Dataset]) -> None:
    """Check a step's inputs, raising on the first disagreement.

    Every disagreement is found before anything is raised, so the raised
    error's `errors` attribute holds all of them. Nothing is computed.

    Args:
        step: The step's name, used in the messages.
        bindings: The step's inputs, by the name the step knows each by.

    Raises:
        CheckError: If any two inputs disagree. The subclass says what kind
            of disagreement it is: `ContigNamingError`, `ContigOrderError`
            or `UndeclaredDimensionError`, all of which are
            `DimensionError`s.
    """
    errors = dimension_errors(step, bindings)
    if errors:
        raise errors[0]

def dimension_errors(step: str, bindings: Mapping[str, Dataset]) -> list[CheckError]:
    """Return every dimension disagreement among a step's inputs.

    One step on its own, for when you are not building a pipeline. A whole
    pipeline is checked with `lg.Pipeline(...).check()`, which also knows
    what each step requires of the ones before it.

    Args:
        step: The step's name, used in the messages.
        bindings: The step's inputs, by the name the step knows each by.

    Returns:
        One error per disagreement, most general first. Empty if the step's
        inputs are consistent. Every error carries the full list in its
        `errors` attribute.
    """
    inputs = [(name, data._core) for name, data in bindings.items()]
    return _build_errors(_core.check_step(step, inputs))

class Dataset:
    """Data of a known kind, carrying the dimensions inferred from it."""

    __slots__ = ("_core",)

    def __init__(self, core: _core.Dataset) -> None:
        """Wrap a dataset loaded by the core engine."""
        self._core = core

    @property
    def kind(self) -> str:
        """The name of the kind of data this holds."""
        return self._core.kind

    @property
    def path(self) -> str | None:
        """The file this was loaded from."""
        return self._core.path

    @property
    def file(self) -> str:
        """The file this data is, for code that has to open it.

        `path` is the honest answer to "where did this come from, if
        anywhere?", so it can be `None` — a step's output carries dimensions
        worked out before anything ran, and has no file of its own until it
        does. This is the answer for the other question, the one a
        `lg.write` body asks:

            return lg.write(lambda out: interpret(v.file, out))

        Inside that function the steps above have run, so there is a file,
        and saying so in the type is what keeps a body from having to prove
        it.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If this data has no file behind it at all.
        """
        found = self._core.path
        if found is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"this {self.kind} has no file behind it, so there is "
                "nothing to open. A step's output has none until the step "
                "has run; `path` is the accessor that admits to that"
            )
        return found

    @property
    def applicable(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """The dimensions that mean anything for this kind of data.

        A dimension outside this set is not a gap to be filled in: asking a
        FASTA for its quality encoding is a category error.
        """
        return tuple(self._core.applicable())

    @property
    def dimensions(self) -> Mapping[str, DimensionValue]:
        """Every dimension that has a known value, by name."""
        found = {}
        for name in self._core.applicable():
            pair = self._core.dimension(name)
            if pair is not None:
                found[name] = DimensionValue(name, pair[0], pair[1])
        return MappingProxyType(found)

    def dimension(self, name: str) -> DimensionValue | None:
        """One dimension's value, or None if it is unknown or inapplicable."""
        pair = self._core.dimension(name)
        if pair is None:
            return None
        return DimensionValue(name, pair[0], pair[1])

    def unknown_reason(self, name: str) -> str | None:
        """Why an applicable dimension has no value.

        None when the dimension is known, or when it does not apply to this
        kind of data at all.
        """
        return self._core.unknown_reason(name)

    @property
    def contigs(self) -> list[Contig] | None:
        """The contigs of the reference this data is on, in file order."""
        contigs = self._core.contigs()
        if contigs is None:
            return None
        return [Contig(name, length, md5) for name, length, md5 in contigs]

    @property
    def samples(self) -> list[str] | None:
        """The samples this data covers, in order."""
        return self._core.samples()

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Identify the dataset by kind and origin."""
        where = self.path or "<in memory>"
        return f"<{type(self).__name__} {self.kind} {where}>"

class Samples:
    """The samples a glob matched, in the order their files appeared.

    Iterable, indexable and sized, so it can be used as an ordinary sequence
    of `Reads`. `map` is the part the golden example uses.
    """

    __slots__ = ("_samples",)

    def __init__(self, samples: list[Reads]) -> None:
        """Hold loaded reads, one entry per sample."""
        self._samples = samples

    @property
    def ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Each sample's identifier, in order.

        Taken from the filenames, with any mate marker removed, unless the
        reads were loaded with the identifier declared.
        """
        return tuple(_identify(sample) for sample in self._samples)

    def map(self, build: Callable[[Reads], T]) -> list[T]:
        """Apply a chain of steps to every sample.

        Nothing is executed. `build` is called once per sample and returns
        whatever the last step in the chain returns — a handle, not data —
        so the result is one output per sample, ready for `lg.Pipeline`.

        Args:

        Returns:

class StepOutput:
    """A handle on data a step would produce.

    Returned by calling a `Step`. It holds no data and has never touched a
    file; what it knows is which step would make it, and from what. Once a
    `Pipeline` has been built from it, `dataset` holds the dimensions the
    engine propagated — the dimensions the output *will* have, worked out
    without running anything.

    Attributes:
        step: The step that would produce it.
        arguments: Everything the step was called with, by parameter name.
    """

    __slots__ = ("_graph", "_node", "_produced", "arguments", "step")

    def __init__(self, step: Step[Any, Any], arguments: dict[str, object]) -> None:
        """Record a deferred call."""
        self.step = step
        self.arguments = arguments
        self._graph: _core.Graph | None = None
        self._node: int | None = None
        self._produced: str | None = None

    @property
    def kind(self) -> str:
        """The kind of data the step declares it produces."""
        return self.step.output

    @property
    def dataset(self) -> Dataset | None:
        """The propagated output dataset, once a `Pipeline` has been built.

        `None` before that: propagation is the graph's work, and there is no
        graph until a pipeline asks for one.
        """
        if self._graph is None or self._node is None:
            return None
        found = self._graph.dataset(self._node)
        if found is None:
            return None
        return KINDS.get(self.kind, Dataset)(found)

    @property
    def file(self) -> str:
        """Where the output is, once the step has produced it.

        The same name `Dataset.file` has, because a body cannot tell which
        it was handed: a step's input is loaded data for the first step of a
        pipeline and another step's handle after that. A `lg.write` body
        reads it inside the function it hands back, by which time the engine
        has run whatever comes above it:

            return lg.write(lambda out: interpret(v.file, out))

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: Before the step has run, when there is no file to
                name. A shell command should use `{placeholders}` instead,
                which the engine fills in for it.
        """
        if self._produced is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"step `{self.step.name}` has not produced anything yet, so "
                "its output has no file. A shell command names its inputs "
                "with placeholders and lets the engine fill them in; a "
                "`lg.write` body reads `.file` inside the function it "
                "returns, which runs after the steps above it"
            )
        return self._produced

    def inputs(self) -> tuple[tuple[Parameter, object], ...]:
        """The data arguments, paired with the parameters they filled."""
        return tuple(
            (parameter, self.arguments[parameter.name])
            for parameter in self.step.dataset_parameters
        )

    def _attach(self, graph: _core.Graph, node: int) -> None:
        self._graph = graph
        self._node = node

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Identify the handle by the step that would produce it."""
        return f"<StepOutput {self.kind} from step `{self.step.name}`>"

docs.title: ligase
docs.text:
Ligase: type-safe, reproducible computational biology pipelines.

Biological data types carry dimensions (organism, reference build, coordinate system, sample set), and the engine refuses to connect steps whose dimensions do not match -- like units in physics.

>>> import ligase as lg
>>> from ligase.types import Alignment, Reads, Reference
>>> hxb2 = lg.reference("refs/HXB2.fasta", organism="HIV-1", build="HXB2")
>>> samples = lg.samples("data/*.fastq.gz", paired=True)
>>> @lg.step(tool="minimap2")
... def align(reads: Reads, ref: Reference) -> Alignment: ...
>>> pipe = lg.Pipeline(samples.map(lambda s: align(s, hxb2)))
>>> pipe.check()   # type-checks every step; nothing runs
>>> pipe.run()     # parallel, cached, per-sample fan-out

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Methods:
    """How a set of results was produced.

    Attributes:
        steps: Each distinct way a step was run, in the order the pipeline
            runs them.
        gaps: Steps nothing is known about.
        references: Every reference any step was given, pinned, with no
            duplicates.
        citations: The reference list, as a methods section prints it.
        uncited: Tools with nothing to cite — named rather than omitted, so
            a short reference list cannot pass for a complete one.
        engine: The version of Ligase that produced the results.
        platform: The platform they were produced on.
        summary: One line — `12 steps, all accounted for.`
        text: The paragraph and the reference list, as the command line
            prints them.
        bundle: The bundle written, where one was asked for.
        verification: What checking a bundle found, where one was asked for.
    """

    steps: list[StepMethods] = field(default_factory=list)
    gaps: list[MethodsGap] = field(default_factory=list)
    references: list[PinnedReference] = field(default_factory=list)
    citations: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    uncited: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    engine: str = ""
    platform: str = ""
    summary: str = ""
    text: str = ""
    bundle: Bundle | None = None
    verification: Verification | None = None

    @property
    def accounted_for(self) -> bool:
        """Whether every step's production is recorded.

        False means the paragraph has a hole in it and says so.
        """
        return not self.gaps

    @property
    def tools(self) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
        """Every tool any step used, with the version it ran at."""
        seen: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        for step in self.steps:
            for tool in step.tools:
                if tool not in seen:
                    seen.append(tool)
        return sorted(seen)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Identify the methods section by its summary."""
        return f"<Methods {self.summary}>"

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Verification:
    """What checking a bundle against this machine found.

    Attributes:
        results: Every result the bundle recorded.
        inputs: Every input it recorded.
        reproduced: Whether every recorded result came out the same.
        verdict: The worst thing found.
        summary: One line — `12 results: 4 identical, 8 reproduced.`
        text: The whole report as the command line prints it.
    """

    results: list[ResultCheck] = field(default_factory=list)
    inputs: list[InputCheck] = field(default_factory=list)
    reproduced: bool = False
    verdict: str = MISSING
    summary: str = ""
    text: str = ""

    @property
    def differing(self) -> list[ResultCheck]:
        """The results that did not come out the same."""
        return [check for check in self.results if not check.reproduced]

    @property
    def moved(self) -> list[InputCheck]:
        """The inputs that are not the ones the bundle was built from.

        Worth reading before any `differs` verdict: a changed input explains
        a changed output, and a bundle cannot fetch its own data.
        """
        return [check for check in self.inputs if check.presence != SAME]

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Identify the verification by its summary."""
        return f"<Verification {self.summary}>"

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AuditReport:
    """What an audit found.

    Attributes:
        steps: Every node audited, in graph order.
        failures: Every node that could not be audited because it failed.
        verdict: The worst verdict any node got — the worst rather than the
            commonest, since one irreproducible sample in a cohort is an
            irreproducible step.
        summary: One line — `4 steps: 1 deterministic, 3 reproducible.`
        text: The whole report as the command line prints it, worded by the
            engine so that every surface reads the same.
    """

    steps: list[StepAudit] = field(default_factory=list)
    failures: list[StepFailure] = field(default_factory=list)
    verdict: str = DETERMINISTIC
    summary: str = ""
    text: str = ""

    @property
    def reproducible(self) -> bool:
        """Whether every node audited agreed with itself."""
        return all(step.reproducible for step in self.steps) and not self.failures

    @property
    def unreproducible(self) -> list[StepAudit]:
        """The nodes whose two runs disagreed about the result."""
        return [step for step in self.steps if not step.reproducible]

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Identify the report by its summary."""
        return f"<AuditReport {self.summary}>"

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class RunReport:
    """Everything a run did.

    Attributes:
        steps: Every step that produced an output, in graph order.
        failures: Every step that did not.
        summary: One line — `12 steps: 8 ran, 4 from cache.` — counting
            places rather than names, since one written step is many steps
            under fan-out.
        text: The whole report as the command line prints it, worded by the
            engine so that every surface reads the same.
        hashed: Input files that had to be read and hashed.
        prefiltered: Input files whose hash was already known from their
            size and mtime, and so were not read at all.
        canonicalised: Files that had to be parsed to find out what they
            mean. Like `hashed`, this is zero on a run that found everything
            it needed already known.
    """

    steps: list[StepRun] = field(default_factory=list)
    failures: list[StepFailure] = field(default_factory=list)
    summary: str = ""
    text: str = ""
    hashed: int = 0
    prefiltered: int = 0
    canonicalised: int = 0

    @property
    def ran(self) -> list[StepRun]:
        """The steps that actually ran, in graph order."""
        return [step for step in self.steps if step.outcome == "ran"]

    @property
    def cached(self) -> list[StepRun]:
        """The steps that were served from the cache."""
        return [step for step in self.steps if step.outcome == "cached"]

    @property
    def skipped(self) -> list[StepRun]:
        """The steps an upstream rerun turned out not to change."""
        return [step for step in self.steps if step.outcome == "skipped"]

    def outputs(self, step: str) -> list[str]:
        """Where one step's outputs are, in graph order.

        Args:
            step: The step's name. Under fan-out there is one output per
                sample.

        Returns:
            One path per node of that name.
        """
        return [run.output for run in self.steps if run.step == step]

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Identify the report by its summary."""
        return f"<RunReport {self.summary}>"

One step that produced an output.

Attributes:

Name Type Description step str

The step's name.

sample str | None

The sample it was for, or None for a step that spans more than one — naming such a step after one of its samples would send you to the wrong data.

outcome str

ran, cached, or skipped. skipped is early cutoff: the step's key was already known although something above it reran, because that rerun produced the same output as before.

output str

Where the output is, in the content-addressed store.

key str

The cache key, as hex.

hash str

The hash of the output's bytes, as hex, which is also its name in the store.

canonical str

The hash of what the output means, as hex: its records sorted and its volatile headers stripped. This is what the steps below were keyed on, so two runs that agree here skip everything downstream however far their bytes diverged.

duration_ms int

How long it took, when it ran; zero otherwise.

node int

Which node of the graph it was.

notes tuple[str, ...]

What was noticed about this output and its hash cannot say — one sentence each, and usually none. A note is not a failure: the step ran and its result stands.

Two things put them here. Canonicalising the output finds the first kind, of which there is one in v0.1: a sample identifier that is a file name rather than a sample, which makes this output's canonical hash depend on where that file was. The step's own body says the second kind — an assumption its work rested on, which the file it wrote need not show. A resistance reading made without coverage is taking every position the caller did not report to be reference, and says so here (D32).

class StepRun:
    """One step that produced an output.

    Attributes:
        step: The step's name.
        sample: The sample it was for, or `None` for a step that spans more
            than one — naming such a step after one of its samples would
            send you to the wrong data.
        outcome: `ran`, `cached`, or `skipped`. `skipped` is early cutoff:
            the step's key was already known although something above it
            reran, because that rerun produced the same output as before.
        output: Where the output is, in the content-addressed store.
        key: The cache key, as hex.
        hash: The hash of the output's bytes, as hex, which is also its name
            in the store.
        canonical: The hash of what the output *means*, as hex: its records
            sorted and its volatile headers stripped. This is what the steps
            below were keyed on, so two runs that agree here skip everything
            downstream however far their bytes diverged.
        duration_ms: How long it took, when it ran; zero otherwise.
        node: Which node of the graph it was.
        notes: What was noticed about this output and its hash cannot say —
            one sentence each, and usually none. A note is not a failure:
            the step ran and its result stands.

            Two things put them here. Canonicalising the output finds the
            first kind, of which there is one in v0.1: a sample identifier
            that is a file name rather than a sample, which makes this
            output's canonical hash depend on where that file was. The
            step's own body says the second kind — an assumption its work
            rested on, which the file it wrote need not show. A resistance
            reading made without coverage is taking every position the
            caller did not report to be reference, and says so here (D32).
    """

    sample: str | None
    outcome: str
    output: str
    key: str
    hash: str
    canonical: str
    duration_ms: int
    node: int

    def ran(self) -> bool:
        """Whether this step actually ran, rather than being served."""
        return self.outcome == "ran"

docs.title: ligase
docs.text:
Ligase: type-safe, reproducible computational biology pipelines.

Biological data types carry dimensions (organism, reference build, coordinate system, sample set), and the engine refuses to connect steps whose dimensions do not match -- like units in physics.

>>> import ligase as lg
>>> from ligase.types import Alignment, Reads, Reference
>>> hxb2 = lg.reference("refs/HXB2.fasta", organism="HIV-1", build="HXB2")
>>> samples = lg.samples("data/*.fastq.gz", paired=True)
>>> @lg.step(tool="minimap2")
... def align(reads: Reads, ref: Reference) -> Alignment: ...
>>> pipe = lg.Pipeline(samples.map(lambda s: align(s, hxb2)))
>>> pipe.check()   # type-checks every step; nothing runs
>>> pipe.run()     # parallel, cached, per-sample fan-out

class CheckError(Exception):
    """A pipeline will not work, found before anything ran.

    Attributes:
        step: The step the problem was found in.
        dimension: The name of the dimension involved, where one is. `None`
            for a `StepTypeError`, which blames no dimension.
        scope: What distinguishes that step from the others of the same name,
            as a `(kind, value)` pair — `("sample", "SRR32217714")` under
            per-sample fan-out. `None` for a step that stands for no single
            sample, such as one that spans a whole cohort. Collecting these
            is how you ask which samples a problem affects:

                affected = {e.scope[1] for e in pipe.errors() if e.scope}

        errors: Every problem found in the same pass, this one included.
            Checking reports all of them at once rather than one per run,
            because fixing errors one per overnight run is the problem
            Ligase exists to remove.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        message: str,
        step: str,
        dimension: str | None,
        scope: tuple[str, str] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Record a problem, its step, its dimension and which step it was."""
        super().__init__(message)
        self.step = step
        self.dimension = dimension
        self.scope = scope
        self.errors: list[CheckError] = []

class RunError(Exception):
    """A step failed.

    Attributes:
        report: The whole run, including everything that did succeed —
            which for a cohort is usually most of it.
        failures: The steps that failed, as a shortcut.
    """

    def __init__(self, report: RunReport) -> None:
        """Carry the whole report, not just the first failure."""
        self.report = report
        self.failures = report.failures
        first = report.failures[0] if report.failures else None
        where = "" if first is None else f"step `{first.step}`: {first.message}"
        super().__init__(f"{report.summary} {where}".strip())
